title: What If You Could Talk to Animals?

shots.line: So... could animals really talk?
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT title: IS ANY OF THIS REAL?

shots.line: In a way, they already do.
shots.scene: Animal icons with sound waves

shots.line: Remember the prairie dogs? That's real.
shots.scene: A prairie dog on lookout

shots.line: A biologist in Arizona spent years recording their alarm calls.
shots.scene: REAL: biologist with a microphone in the desert

shots.line: They don't just shout "danger".
shots.scene: A call labelled DANGER, crossed out

shots.line: They describe what's coming: a person, how tall, even the colour of their shirt.
shots.scene: Different waves for a tall / short person and shirt colours

shots.line: Vervet monkeys have different alarms for a leopard, an eagle and a snake.
shots.scene: Three alarms: leopard, eagle, snake

shots.line: Hear "eagle", and they look up.
shots.scene: Monkeys look up, eagle above

shots.line: Hear "snake", and they look down.
shots.scene: Monkeys look down, snake below

shots.line: Honeybees dance to tell each other which way the flowers are, and how far.
shots.scene: The waggle dance on the comb, angle to the sun, flowers

shots.line: That dance won a Nobel Prize in nineteen seventy-three.
shots.scene: NOBEL PRIZE 1973 medal

shots.line: And in twenty twenty-four, scientists in Kenya found that wild elephants have names too.
shots.scene: KENYA savanna: elephants

shots.line: Play an elephant a call meant for her, and she calls back.
shots.scene: A call for her: she turns and calls back

shots.line: Meant for someone else? She mostly ignores it.
shots.scene: A call for someone else: she keeps eating

shots.line: And here's one the internet gets wrong: one dog year isn't seven human years.
shots.scene: 1 DOG YEAR = 7 HUMAN YEARS, crossed out

shots.line: A twenty twenty study of Labradors' DNA worked out that a fourteen-year-old dog is about seventy-three.
shots.scene: DNA helix and the curve; 14 -> 73

shots.line: Biscuit is seventy-three.
shots.scene: Biscuit in his sunny spot, badge 73

shots.line: Right now, a team called Project CETI is using AI to decode the clicks of sperm whales.
shots.scene: Underwater: a sperm whale, clicks as dots; PROJECT CETI

shots.line: They've already found patterns in them, like an alphabet.
shots.scene: Click patterns laid out like an alphabet

shots.line: None of these animals talk the way we do.
shots.scene: All the animals side by side

shots.line: But every one of them is saying something.
shots.scene: Bubbles over each animal

shots.line: We just never learned how to listen.
shots.scene: You, listening

shots.line: Remember the whales. You're going to hear them again.
shots.scene: The whale glows; back to the story

shots.scene: Underwater: a mother whale and her calf
